title: Integration and End-to-End Tests knowledge check

questions.prompt: Which test strategy provides stronger evidence than a single passing happy-path example?
options: Test expected behavior, edge cases and failure paths, and add type-level tests for public type contracts where useful.
Only measure line coverage and assume that proves correctness.
Mock every component so no integration is ever checked.
questions.answer_key: Test expected behavior, edge cases and failure paths, and add type-level tests for public type contracts where useful.
questions.explanation: Coverage is a signal, not proof; test quality depends on assertions, cases and realistic boundaries.

questions.prompt: Which statement is correct about “Integration and End-to-End Tests”?
options: The safest approach is to skip diagnostics and trust the first output.
A type assertion automatically validates every value at runtime.
The learner should publish hidden solutions so the exercise can grade itself.
The concept should be demonstrated with testing interconnected components and checked against its intended contract.
questions.answer_key: The concept should be demonstrated with testing interconnected components and checked against its intended contract.
questions.explanation: The supplied syllabus explicitly includes “Testing interconnected components”; connect it to a concrete example and verify the behavior relevant to this lesson.

questions.prompt: What is a good verification step after practicing “Integration and End-to-End Tests”?
options: Ignore compiler or test failures if the interface looks correct.
Treat passing a static token check as proof that the program executed correctly.
Check api and database integration, include a meaningful failure case where appropriate, and document any runtime or version assumptions.
Assume validating real user workflows is unnecessary because the code has type annotations.
questions.answer_key: Check api and database integration, include a meaningful failure case where appropriate, and document any runtime or version assumptions.
questions.explanation: The syllabus includes “API and database integration”. Verification should match the concept: type-level checks, runtime tests, configuration checks or human review as appropriate.
